title: Kethanahalli Falls
tagline: Bengaluru → Devanahalli → Chikkaballapur → Kethanahalli Falls. ~78 km, a monsoon waterfall at the end of a rough rocky trail.
summary: Kethanahalli Falls, also called Vivekananda Falls, is a seasonal two-tier waterfall of roughly 90 ft tucked among the hills north of Chikkaballapur. The ride up NH 44 is easy highway; the fun starts past Kethanahalli village, where farm tracks give way to a moderately tough off-road trail of loose rock, steep ruts and slick patches. The falls only really run during and after the monsoon — outside that window you may find a dry rock face.

segments.note: City exit and the fast airport highway to Devanahalli.
Four-lane highway past the Nandi Hills turn-off to Chikkaballapur.

segments.road: Village roads via Kethanahalli, then trail
segments.note: ~17 km of rural roads to Kethanahalli village, then a rough trail of loose rock, steep ruts and slick ground; the last ~1 km to the falls is on foot.

highlights: Two-tier seasonal waterfall, ~90 ft, roaring in the monsoon
Ringed by the Nandi group of hills — Brahmagiri, Skandagiri, Divyagiri and others
A genuine off-road trail barely an hour and a half from the city
Countryside to rock-garden transition makes it good ADV practice

offroad.summary: Moderately tough: loose rocks, steep rutted climbs and slick sections that get much harder when wet.
notes: Trail is unmarked; locals in Kethanahalli are the best guide to the way in
Wet rock and mud in the monsoon — exactly when the falls flow — make it slippery
The final stretch to the falls is not rideable; park and walk ~1 km
Knobby or dual-sport tyres strongly recommended

timings: Free entry; usually listed as ~7 am – 5 pm
Falls flow only during and shortly after the monsoon (roughly Jun – Oct/Nov); can be dry otherwise
Fuel up in Chikkaballapur — nothing beyond the town
No food at the falls; eat in Chikkaballapur
cautions: Risky solo — ride with at least one other bike
Leopards and sloth bears are reported in the surrounding hills; don't linger after dusk
Flash flow after heavy rain — stay off the rocks at the lip of the falls
